items.name: TIFF 2028: Canadian features (world premiere target)
items.amount: Best Canadian Feature Film Award C$10,000; Best Canadian Discovery Award C$10,000 (first or second Canadian feature)
items.why_fit: The most valuable launch for a Toronto first feature: Canadian press, buyers and Telefilm all watch TIFF, and the Best Canadian Discovery Award is reserved for first and second features. In 2026 Serville Poblete's Sunburn, a Filipino-Canadian Toronto indie, won TIFF's Best Canadian Feature Film award.
items.priorities: TIFF programmes world, international and North American premieres; it may accept a film with only a Canadian premiere, but premiere status is weighed in final programming decisions.
items.eligibility: Features of 60+ minutes completed in the year before the festival (2026 edition: on or after 4 Sept 2025); not released in North America in theatres, on TV, streaming, DVD/Blu-ray or VOD; never submitted to TIFF before. Non-English films need English subtitles; English-language films need English closed captions. FilmFreeway only.
items.watch_out: Premiere status decides this one. A public screening in early January 2028 in Toronto would use up PURPLE's world premiere and, because it is in Canada, its Canadian premiere too, which in practice rules out TIFF 2028. Keep the January screening private (invite-only cast, crew, funders and family; no tickets, no public listing, no press or reviews, no festival) and confirm with TIFF's submissions team before it happens. A film can be submitted to TIFF only once, so do not send an early rough cut. 2026 to 2028 fees could not be confirmed (tiff.net blocks automated reading).

items.amount: Grand Jury Prize, jury awards and Audience Award (no cash published)

A January 2028 screening in Canada does not break international premiere status (only screenings outside Canada count), and neither would TIFF, but Sundance rarely takes films that have played TIFF, and any festival outside Canada first (Giffoni, Busan, LAAPFF) would end eligibility. Very competitive.

items.name: SXSW Film & TV Festival: narrative features

items.premiere: Not stated on the submissions page; confirm in the SXSW FAQ.

Screenings in Canada (January 2028, TIFF) are fine because Generation takes international premieres; any European screening first (for example Giffoni) would end eligibility. items.premiere: World premieres preferred; Generation accepts international and European premieres; festival screenings or release in the country of origin are accepted; no German premieres.
